stories.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 to the public and Mythos 5 to trusted cyber partners

key_facts.fact: Anthropic on June 9, 2026 launched Claude Fable 5, its first Mythos-class model cleared for general use, alongside Claude Mythos 5, the same underlying model with cyber safeguards lifted and available only to a small group of vetted cyberdefenders through Project Glasswing.

Fable 5 ships with classifiers that route queries on cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, and model distillation to the earlier Claude Opus 4.8 model, with the user notified; Anthropic says fallback triggers in fewer than 5% of sessions.
Mythos 5 scored 78% on the ExploitBench cybersecurity benchmark, nearly double Claude Opus 4.8's 40% and above the 69% from the earlier Mythos Preview.
On Vellum's breakdown, Fable 5 scored 80.3% on SWE-Bench Pro versus 69.2% for Opus 4.8 and 58.6% for GPT-5.5, and ranks #1 on the Hebbia Finance senior-analyst benchmark.
After more than 1,000 hours of red-team testing through an external bug bounty, Anthropic says no universal jailbreaks were found for Fable 5.
Fable 5 API pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, roughly 2x Claude Opus 4.8 input and roughly 2x GPT-5.5 sticker input price.
Fable 5 is included on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans at no extra cost through June 22, 2026, after which usage credits will be required.

stories.headline: Trump administration tells CAISI to stop publishing AI model evaluations

key_facts.fact: Trump administration officials told the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) to halt publication of its frontier AI model assessments while the June 2 executive order is implemented, the Wall Street Journal first reported.

National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross directly ordered CAISI to stop publishing its model assessments, citing national security concerns; the directive does not end CAISI's testing or its voluntary agreements with AI developers, only the public output.

The June 2, 2026 executive order creates a voluntary framework for AI companies to share frontier models with the federal government up to 30 days before public release to 'promote secure innovation and strengthen the cybersecurity of critical infrastructure.'
The order assigns the classified benchmarking process to the Treasury Department, the NSA and CISA, with the NSA director determining when a model qualifies as a 'covered frontier model.'

Within the agency, the halt drew criticism as an attempt by Cairncross to widen his influence over evaluations; OpenAI raised CAISI's importance with the administration, while White House AI advisers including David Sacks have warned that excessive verification could slow deployment.

organizations: Center for AI Standards and Innovation

stories.headline: EU orders Meta to give rival AI chatbots free access to WhatsApp via emergency interim measure

key_facts.fact: The European Commission on June 9 ordered Meta to give competing AI assistants free access to WhatsApp under emergency interim measures while it completes an antitrust investigation, the second time the EU has used the emergency power in over 20 years

Meta has until June 15 to restore rivals' access to the WhatsApp for Business API on the same terms that applied before October 2025, when it began restricting AI rivals while exempting its own Meta AI assistant

If Meta ignores the order it could face fines of up to 10% of annual global revenue, or roughly $20 billion based on its 2025 earnings; the interim measure can last until June 2029 or until the investigation concludes

The investigation followed complaints from The Interaction Company of California (developer of Poke.com), French AI startup Agentik and a Spanish rival; Meta said it will appeal, calling it 'regulatory overreach'
Italy folded its near-identical probe into the EU investigation a day before the decision; Brazil's regulator had already forced Meta to reopen access there in March

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, a real-time speech-to-speech model covering 70+ languages

key_facts.fact: Google on June 9, 2026 released Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, an audio-to-audio model that auto-detects more than 70 languages and generates continuously streamed translated speech preserving the speaker's intonation, pacing and pitch.
Unlike turn-based systems, the model speaks continuously and stays just a few seconds behind the original speaker, avoiding the long pauses traditional speech translation produces.

It is rolling out today in the Google Translate app on Android and iOS, in public preview for developers through the Gemini Live API and Google AI Studio, and in private preview to select Google Workspace customers via Google Meet.
In Google Meet the model raises supported languages from 5 to 70+, enabling more than 2,000 language combinations in a single meeting, versus the prior limit of translating only to and from English.
The Translate Android app also gains a new 'listening mode' that pipes translations through the phone's earpiece without headphones, treating the device like a regular call.
The developer model code is gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview with an input token limit of 131,072 and output token limit of 65,536; audio output is watermarked with SynthID.

stories.headline: Meta partners with Reliance on first India AI data center: 168 MW in Jamnagar, Gujarat

key_facts.fact: Meta and Reliance Industries announced an agreement on June 10 for Meta's first AI-enabled data center in India, with Reliance building a 168 MW facility in Jamnagar, Gujarat that Meta will lease.
The facility will be powered by renewable energy and cooled with desalinated seawater; Meta will cover the full cost of the energy and water supporting the facility.
Reliance said the 168 MW facility will be ready within two years and can be expanded over time, also supporting Meta's global infrastructure and AI computing requirements.
Separately, Meta contracted nearly 1 GW of renewable energy capacity in India through agreements with CleanMax and Fourth Partner Energy.
The deal builds on Meta's $5.7B 2020 investment in Reliance's Jio Platforms and a $100M joint venture last year on enterprise AI solutions.

stories.headline: OpenAI in advanced talks to lease a 10GW Ohio data center with Nvidia credit support

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is in advanced negotiations to lease a proposed 10-gigawatt data center campus on federal land in southern Ohio, in a deal that could include financial backing from Nvidia, The Information reported June 9, 2026.
Fully built out, the campus could cost at least $500 billion based on current chip, labor, power and materials prices.
OpenAI is expected to sign a 20-year lease and take over payments once the project starts operating; the first ~800MW phase is targeted to launch in 2028.
Nvidia is in discussions to provide credit support by guaranteeing OpenAI's lease rather than investing directly, acting as a de facto infrastructure financier to lock in long-term chip demand.
The site is being developed by SB Energy, a SoftBank unit, on US Department of Energy land in southern Ohio.

stories.headline: Seattle City Council votes 9-0 for one-year moratorium on new large data centers

key_facts.fact: The Seattle City Council voted unanimously on June 9 to impose a one-year emergency moratorium on new large data centers inside city limits.
The ordinance halts applications for data centers with electrical capacity above 20 megavolt-amperes (roughly 20 MW), enough power for thousands of homes.
Mayor Katie Wilson is expected to sign the legislation; the moratorium can be extended for an additional six months and a public hearing must be held within 60 days.
Proposed data center projects in Seattle reportedly had combined peak demand equal to about a third of the city's average daily power consumption.
The ordinance exempts roughly 30 smaller data centers already operating in Seattle, allowing each to expand by up to another 20 megavolt-amperes.

stories.headline: SK Hynix targets US ADR listing as soon as August, potentially raising up to $14B

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix plans to list its shares in the US as soon as August, seeking to capitalize on AI-stock appetite and broaden its investor base, sources told Reuters.
The SEC is expected to approve SK Hynix's American depositary receipt (ADR) listing application during the week of June 22.
SK Hynix filed confidentially in March, with the offering potentially raising as much as $14B.
SK Hynix is the world's second-largest memory chipmaker and a key Nvidia supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips used in AI servers.
SK Hynix stock has jumped 240% year-to-date and its market cap has surpassed $1 trillion.

stories.headline: SoftBank's $6B margin loan against its OpenAI stake stalls with creditors

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Group's talks with potential creditors to raise at least $6 billion through a margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake have stalled, Bloomberg reported, weeks after SoftBank cut the target from an original $10 billion.
Before the talks stalled, SoftBank had secured roughly $5 billion in commitments, though it was unclear whether those were verbal or written.

Lenders balked at valuing exposure tied to OpenAI, which is private, and reportedly cited reports of OpenAI missing some internal sales and user milestones in recent quarters; the loan was structured with a two-year term and a one-year extension option.
The stalled talks come one day after OpenAI said it had confidentially filed for a US IPO; SoftBank also still faces a $40 billion bridge loan repayment due in 2027.
SoftBank says it is considering various fundraising options and could still revive the margin loan at a later stage.

stories.headline: SoftBank's $6B margin loan backed by OpenAI stake stalls as lenders balk at valuation

key_facts.fact: SoftBank's talks with potential creditors to raise at least $6 billion through a margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake have stalled, just weeks after the conglomerate cut its initial target from $10 billion
SoftBank had secured about $5 billion in commitments before talks stalled, though it was unclear whether those were verbal or written; the company is now considering alternative fundraising options

Some prospective creditors balked at valuing OpenAI as collateral and at reports the startup had missed internal sales and user milestones; the loan was structured with a two-year term plus one-year extension option
The stall comes one day after OpenAI confidentially filed for a US IPO, and as SoftBank still faces a $40 billion bridge loan repayment due in 2027

stories.headline: SpaceX IPO draws $250B+ in investor demand, nearly 4x oversubscribed at $75B target

key_facts.fact: SpaceX has drawn more than $250 billion of investor demand for what is poised to be the largest-ever IPO, dwarfing the $75 billion it is seeking to raise
The deal's oversubscription rate is running at three-and-a-half to four times the planned offering size, with long-only funds placing sizable orders
SpaceX has set a price of $135 per share for the IPO, valuing the company at $1.77 trillion; pricing is expected June 11 with trading to begin June 12 on Nasdaq

On June 9, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and finance chief Bret Johnsen were scheduled to attend a Morgan Stanley lunch with about 300 institutional investors; Musk briefly joined some Zoom meetings

stories.headline: Standard Bots raises $200M Series C at $1B valuation to scale US-made AI robot arms

key_facts.fact: Standard Bots announced on June 9 a $200M Series C led by RoboStrategy and existing investor General Catalyst at a $1 billion valuation.
The round is a significant step up from the $63M Standard Bots raised in 2024 at an undisclosed valuation.
The company makes AI-native robot arms and industrial humanoids deployed at customers including Sunoco, Amazon, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the US Army.
The capital will fund expansion of the Glen Cove, New York manufacturing facility; the company plans by 2027 to manufacture everything 'from metal in to robots out' in the US.
Standard Bots' robots are taught by demonstration rather than code, with AI running in the background to learn tasks.

stories.headline: Super Micro plans $7B equity raise to fund $39B in AI server component purchases

key_facts.fact: Super Micro announced a $7.0 billion series of concurrent equity and equity-linked financing transactions on June 9, 2026 to fund AI server component purchases.
The package consists of a $1.25B common stock offering, a $3.75B depositary share offering, and a $2B at-the-market program starting no earlier than Q3 2026.
Proceeds will fund components for approximately $39 billion of recent AI server orders from more than 20 customers.
SMCI shares fell 8% in extended trading on dilution concerns despite the order backlog.

stories.headline: Tata chairman says TCS will soon have as many AI agents as its 600,000 employees, hiring to slow

key_facts.fact: Tata chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran said at TCS's June 9 annual general meeting that the IT services giant will soon have as many AI agents as human employees, with the company plans to reduce hiring as AI use accelerates

TCS is India's largest private-sector employer with around 600,000 staff; its headcount fell by more than 23,000 on a net basis in fiscal year ended March 2026, after cutting more than 12,000 jobs in July 2025
Chandrasekaran predicted TCS will reach AI-agent-to-employee parity within three years and said 100% of TCS revenue will have an AI component before the end of the decade
TCS reported an annualized AI revenue run-rate of $2.4 billion in Q4 fiscal 2026, growing at a 22.4% compound quarterly rate, against the backdrop of India's $315 billion IT services sector

stories.headline: AMD-only cloud TensorWave raises $350M Series B at $1.55B valuation led by AMD and Magnetar

key_facts.fact: Las Vegas-based TensorWave raised $350M in a Series B round led by AMD and hedge fund Magnetar Capital, valuing the company at $1.55B.
The new round nearly quadrupled TensorWave's valuation from roughly $400 million a year earlier.
TensorWave operates an 8,192 AMD Instinct MI325X GPU 'dedicated training' cluster and plans to use the capital to expand data center capacity and buy more chips from AMD.
CEO Darrick Horton said the company was created to 'restore competition to the market' against Nvidia's dominance.

stories.headline: Reuters: Trump family banked $2.3B from four crypto ventures while investors lost the same amount

key_facts.fact: A Reuters investigation found the Trump family generated about $2.3 billion in pretax income from four crypto ventures between November 2024 and April 2026, while more than one million investors absorbed about $2.3 billion in net losses

World Liberty Financial was the largest contributor, channeling more than $1.4 billion to the family through a structure giving DT Marks DEFI LLC a 75% cut of token sale proceeds; WLFI holders sat on roughly $674 million in losses by end of April

The TRUMP meme coin generated roughly $616 million for the family while buyers lost more than $700 million; ALT5 Sigma shareholders lost about $675 million and American Bitcoin investors lost over $200 million

Reuters found no evidence the Trumps invested their own capital; experts said each venture could have been set up for under $1 million in development and legal costs, with gains coming from licensing and revenue sharing
Eight government ethics experts told Reuters the arrangement represents a conflict of interest unlike anything seen in modern American history, though all noted it is legal absent a quid pro quo
